items.title: John Pizzarelli, Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: And Joe Mooney was blind and he had the accordion with Andy Fitzgerald on clarinet and Jack Hotop on guitar and Gate Frega.

ctx.x: Yeah. You’re getting paid to rehearse.

Ear training 101 too. Well we’ll fake that song, okay, and he’d play melodies. And the best example of that is my first gig with my dad was eight weeks at the Pierre Hotel in 1980, the summer of 1980. July and August. And the first night I knew about eight songs. And if I only knew, we had to play four hours. And I remember him saying “Mountain Greenery.” “What?” And he’d go [scats] and he’d look at me and he’d be pounding these melodies out, and wouldn’t tell me anything. And maybe once in a while he’d hit a G7…
Was it aggravating at the time?
